title: Cystic fibrosis with steatorrhea and failure to thrive: decreased fecal elastase (pancreatic insufficiency)
vignette: A 15-month-old boy is brought to the office by his parents for poor weight gain. The parents have also noticed frequent, large, foul-smelling stools. He was admitted to the hospital for a prolonged bout of bacterial pneumonia 6 months ago. Both parents are healthy and have no similar symptoms. The child was born at term at home. He is at the 20th percentile for length and 3rd percentile for weight. Vital signs are normal. On examination, the child appears thin and has a nontender, nondistended abdomen. Which of the following is most likely present in this patient?

clues.note: Bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stools (steatorrhea) indicate FAT malabsorption from pancreatic insufficiency.
Recurrent sinopulmonary infections plus failure to thrive/steatorrhea in a child point to CYSTIC FIBROSIS (with pancreatic insufficiency).

whatMatters: Failure to thrive + STEATORRHEA + recurrent pneumonia in a child = CYSTIC FIBROSIS with PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY. Thick secretions block pancreatic ducts, so exocrine enzyme (including ELASTASE) output falls - producing DECREASED FECAL ELASTASE (an accurate marker of pancreatic insufficiency). Answer B.
strategy: Diagnose CF pancreatic insufficiency (steatorrhea, failure to thrive, recurrent respiratory infections), then pick the confirmatory finding: LOW fecal elastase (a pancreatic enzyme; reduced secretion -> reduced stool level). Reject options that increase or don't fit: decreased fecal calcium (CF causes INCREASED fecal calcium from vitamin-D deficiency), increased fecal calprotectin (inflammatory bowel disease, not CF), increased fecal chymotrypsin (a pancreatic enzyme that DECREASES like elastase), and increased pancreatic bicarbonate (DECREASED in CF, lowering duodenal pH).

eliminations.label: Decreased fecal calcium - actually increased in CF
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: less calcium in stool. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: in CF, vitamin D malabsorption and fat malabsorption INCREASE fecal calcium (calcium binds unabsorbed fatty acids), so fecal calcium is elevated, not decreased. ✅ Correct if: increased calcium absorption (not CF).

eliminations.label: Increased fecal calprotectin - inflammatory bowel disease
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a neutrophil-derived marker of intestinal inflammation (IBD). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: calprotectin is elevated in inflammatory diarrhea (ulcerative colitis, Crohn), not in CF pancreatic insufficiency. ✅ Correct if: inflammatory bowel disease.

eliminations.label: Increased fecal chymotrypsin - decreases with insufficiency
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: another pancreatic digestive enzyme measurable in stool. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: like elastase, chymotrypsin output DECREASES (not increases) with pancreatic insufficiency. ✅ Correct if: adequate pancreatic enzyme secretion.

eliminations.label: Increased pancreatic bicarbonate - decreased in CF
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: more bicarbonate secreted to neutralize gastric acid. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: CFTR dysfunction reduces bicarbonate secretion, LOWERING duodenal pH (which further inactivates enzymes) - the opposite of increased. ✅ Correct if: normal CFTR ductal bicarbonate secretion.

reasoning: Steatorrhea + failure to thrive + recurrent pneumonia = cystic fibrosis with pancreatic insufficiency
Thick secretions obstruct pancreatic ducts, reducing exocrine enzyme output
Elastase is a pancreatic enzyme, so its stool level falls (low fecal elastase)
mechanism: CYSTIC FIBROSIS (CF) is an autosomal recessive disorder (most commonly delta-F508 CFTR mutation) in which a defective chloride channel produces THICK, dehydrated secretions in multiple organs. In the PANCREAS, viscous mucus obstructs ducts and acini, blocking DIGESTIVE ENZYMES from reaching the duodenum and causing progressive inflammation/fibrosis and EXOCRINE PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY (often present at birth or evolving in childhood). Reduced enzyme delivery causes fat/protein malabsorption: STEATORRHEA (bulky, foul-smelling stools), FAILURE TO THRIVE, and fat-soluble vitamin (A, D, E, K) deficiencies; recurrent SINOPULMONARY infections (S aureus, Pseudomonas) reflect airway disease. PANCREATIC ELASTASE is a proenzyme made by acinar cells and activated in the duodenum; because it is decreased when pancreatic secretion falls and is not degraded in transit, LOW FECAL ELASTASE is an accurate, noninvasive marker of pancreatic insufficiency of any cause (CF, chronic pancreatitis). Diagnosis of CF uses an elevated sweat chloride and CFTR genetic testing. The distractors are incorrect: fecal calcium and calprotectin don't fit, and other pancreatic enzymes (chymotrypsin) and ductal bicarbonate DECREASE, not increase.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid GI/Peds > cystic fibrosis: CFTR defect -> thick secretions; pancreatic insufficiency (steatorrhea, failure to thrive, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency); recurrent sinopulmonary infections; low fecal elastase = marker of pancreatic insufficiency; sweat chloride/CFTR testing.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: CF pancreatic insufficiency -> reduced enzyme output -> decreased fecal elastase.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on cystic fibrosis, pancreatic insufficiency, steatorrhea, fecal elastase, or CFTR/bicarbonate? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Fecal calcium/calprotectin don't fit; chymotrypsin and bicarbonate DECREASE (not increase) in insufficiency.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: pancreatic insufficiency (CF) = low fecal elastase; steatorrhea + failure to thrive + recurrent lung infections.

Elevated sweat chloride + CFTR genetic testing
Decreased -> low duodenal pH inactivates enzymes

firstAid.detail: GI: low fecal elastase; steatorrhea/failure to thrive.

memoryHook: CF clogs the pancreas so digestive enzymes can't get out - including elastase, which then shows up LOW in the stool (the marker of pancreatic insufficiency).
